messages:
Alice Park: Quick question — for the scorer endpoint should we require a normalized float (0..1) or allow an int-based score with explicit units? This affects quota math, dashboard buckets, and how we display deltas.
Ben Wu: leaning normalized float. simpler for clients and dashboards. but precision/quantization matters for small diffs.
Carlos M: int-with-units gives us backward compatibility and avoids float comparability issues. e.g., store as milli-units (0..1000) integer.
Dina Li: Analytics: if we mix formats telemetry gets messy. We need a single canonical internal representation for metrics ingestion.
Eva (analytics): Agree with Dina. If we accept multiple encodings we must tag events with score_encoding and maintain converter in pipeline.
Alice Park: ok — practical choices: a) require normalized float and server converts to internal int scale; b) allow 'score_value' + 'score_units' pair and dashboards read units.
Ben Wu: a) is easier for users. b) is more explicit and future-proof. console UX for allowing user to set display units gets trickier with a).
Carlos M: Implementation note: routing policy uses score thresholds for model affinity. Those thresholds currently configured as ints (e.g., >500). Changing to float will require config migration.
Dina Li: canary plan idea: accept both for 3 months, write parser that normalizes to canonical_milli_score on ingress, emit telemetry showing proportion of formats.
Alice Park: good. what about precision? we could normalize to integer milli-score (0..1000 per 0..1), or micros (0..1_000_000) for fine grained.
Ben Wu: micros seems overkill. milli is enough for ranking decisions. saves storage and avoids floating edge cases.
Eva (analytics): Agree milli is fine. Also recommend we store original_raw and canonical_milli in logs for audits.
Carlos M: API example proposal for V2 rescorer:
```
POST /v2/scorer
{
  "candidates": [{"id":"c1","payload":...}],
  // either of the following
  "score_value": 0.827,                // normalized float
  // OR
  "score_value": 827, "score_units":"milli"  // explicit units
}
```
Server then sets canonical_milli = (score_units=="milli") ? score_value : round(score_value*1000)

Dina Li: console/rollouts: add toggle "accept-legacy-units" behind ff/scorer_v2. If ff off then reject int-with-units.
Alice Park: telemetry labels: score_encoding:{"float","milli"}, canonical_milli, parse_errors, ingestion_latency.
Ben Wu: quota implications: we currently bill/reserve on candidate_count and model fanout. If we start using score bands for quota (eg >700 costs more), we must define billing units. Suggest keep billing separate from score for now.
Eva (analytics): dashboard: surface distribution histogram of canonical_milli per route/model. Add toggle to switch display to 0..1 floats. Also add migration widget showing percentage of requests using float vs milli.
Carlos M: model affinity: routing rules will be expressed in canonical_milli thresholds. We'll need migration script to convert existing int configs (they're already milli, right?) to ensure nothing changes.
Ben Wu: final action items: 1) implement ingress normalizer that emits telemetry (Carlos+Ben), 2) add FF & console toggle (Dina+Alice), 3) update routing config migration plan (Carlos), 4) update docs + SDK examples (DevEx).
Alice Park: sounds good. I'll create a tiny PR spec with the API contract and migration steps. tagging people: @Ben, @Carlos, @Dina, @Eva :thumbsup:
